title: Result-changing reuse: curvature estimators, loader normals, grid A*, resampling and the other skipped survey items
description:
The reuse items from MESH-91's duplication survey that were skipped because each one changes results. Each needs a measured before/after, not a mechanical swap. Line numbers are from the survey on master and may have moved.

1. Two curvature estimators in one pipeline: SemanticPatchDecomposer.computeMean/Gaussian/PrincipalCurvatures (Meyer cotangent Laplacian plus angle defect, about 140 lines) runs next to PrincipalDirectionField.compute (1-ring shape operator) on the same mesh (SemanticPatchDecomposer around line 203). Decide which estimator to keep, then measure the patch decomposition, crest and saddle outputs on the test meshes.
2. DisplacementSum.ringSum vs MeshSmoothing.neighbourMean: ringSum counts the vertex itself and is used in sum form; neighbourMean is private. One shared ring average with a count-self option.
3. OBJ/OFF loader normals: ObjMeshParser (~125-165) and OffMeshParser (~334-370) compute identical unit-normal-per-fan-triangle vertex normals and overwrite the area-weighted HalfEdgeMeshOps.computeNormals result MeshLoader.indexedMesh already produced. Dropping them changes shading slightly: compare renders.
4. Grid A*: IrregularQuadGrid.shortestPath and AStarCorridorPathfinder2D/3D.aStar each run their own priority queue; numeric/graph/Dijkstra.relax(node, candidate, priority, via) exists for A*. Tie order may change seeded dungeon output: compare seeded procgen before and after.
5. Arc-length resampling, five copies: BiRailLoftNode.resampleToUniform vs its own resampleArray, BirailLoftMeshNode.resampleArcLength, MeshSkeletonComparator.resampleJoints, and ResampleCurveNode.appendResampled (different spacing rule). One helper; also check whether the birail_loft and bi_rail_loft nodes overlap as a whole.
6. Douglas-Peucker: MeshSkeletonExtractor.rdpSimplify (3D, recursive) vs grid2d/PolylineSimplify.douglasPeucker (2D, iterative); give PolylineSimplify a stride.
7. SVG root writers: MultiviewScreenshot (~338-354) and StrokeSketch.toSvg (~689-715) share a format; TraceOutlines (~168-173) hardcodes the attribute names; both endpoints repeat the cell layout comment.
8. Spatial indexes: MeshDistance.KDTree3D (raw floats, squared distances) vs NearestVertex's grid (mesh-based, refuses near-ties). Partial overlap.
9. Camera projection: StrokeSketch.cellPixel repeats Camera3D.projectToPixels for a given cell size, with a -0.5 pixel-centre difference; Camera3D needs a width/height overload. Check whether SilhouetteHullNode's inner loop can share it without losing speed.
10. The partial SubdivideMeshNode copy of the subdivision code (SubdivideMeshNode vs SubdivisionMeshNode).
definition-of-done: 1. Every item is either consolidated onto one shared implementation or recorded as kept apart with the reason. 2. Each consolidation that changes output has a before/after comparison on the ticket (test meshes, renders or seeded procgen, as the item says). 3. Full test suite passes. 4. A launch entry and screenshot show the most visible change (curvature or shading).
testing-plan: 1. Before each change, capture the affected output on its test inputs. 2. After it, compare and record the difference on the ticket. 3. Run the full suite.
changes-made: Measured with benchmark/ResultChangingReuseBenchmark (new, test/benchmark): it writes every affected output per case to tmp/mesh-92/<run> and, given -Dbenchmark.compare, a summary.tsv row per case. Before-run on master, a repeat run (identical apart from a 0.009 degree acos floor on normals), then after-runs.

Item 2, ringSum vs neighbourMean: kept apart for now. DisplacementSum is in the sculpt/ package, which lands through MESH-91; the shared count-self ring average waits for that to land, then MeshSmoothing.neighbourMean and DisplacementSum.ringSum both call it.

Item 3, loader normals: ObjMeshParser (no vn lines) and OffMeshParser no longer synthesize unit-normal-per-fan-triangle vertex normals; MeshLoader.indexedMesh keeps the mesh's own area-weighted ones. HalfEdgeMeshOps.computeNormals now weighs a polygon by its whole fanned vector area instead of its first three corners, so a quad folded across its first diagonal counts both halves. Before/after vertex normal angle: rocker-arm mean 2.24 / max 25.2 deg; Hand-tri-30k 1.05 / 33.2; fandisk 0.50 / 19.2; hand-quad.obj (fanned to triangles by the OBJ parser) 2.39 / 169.9, the 170 degree vertices sit on folds in the file, triangles facing opposite ways, where the weighting decides; botijo_out_quad_20.off (kept as quads) 9.93 / 52.7.

Item 4, grid A*: AStarCorridorPathfinder2D and 3D and IrregularQuadGrid.shortestPath run on numeric/graph/Dijkstra.relax(node, candidate, priority, via); the 2D search is inlined into carve, the (f, g, index) cellOrder comparator and the O(n) PriorityQueue.remove are gone. Trade maps (IrregularQuadGrid): all six levels' roads and rivers identical, since Dijkstra's heap pops ties as PriorityQueue does. Dungeons: corridors stay optimal but equal-cost routes tie-break by insertion order now, so later corridors reuse different hallways: dungeon_2d seeds 1-12 differ in 4-62 of 900 cells (hallway count -8..+6), dungeon_3d in 37-155 of 4500 (hallway -9..+15, stairs -5..+3).

Item 5, arc-length resampling: new grid2d/PolylineResample.uniform(packed, first, points, stride, closed, samples) replaces BiRailLoftNode.resampleToUniform and resampleArray, BirailLoftMeshNode.resampleArcLength/pointAtArcLength and its nested Polyline class, and MeshSkeletonComparator.resampleJoints. Before/after: birail_loft_ribbon and neck_armor meshes identical, skeleton joint deltas identical. ResampleCurveNode.appendResampled stays apart: it splits each segment into ceil(length/spacing) pieces and keeps every input point (corners), a different rule from even resampling. bi_rail_loft and birail_loft stay two nodes: bi_rail_loft sweeps a normalized, blendable profile between the rails and solidifies; birail_loft is the ruled surface between them.

Item 6, Douglas-Peucker: PolylineSimplify gains keptPoints(packed, stride, tolerance); douglasPeucker(xy) is its stride-2 caller and MeshSkeletonExtractor's recursive rdpSimplify/rdpRecurse are gone. Skeleton joints of hand, rocker-arm and bolt identical before/after.

Item 7, SVG roots: new automation/endpoints/ui/SketchSvgRoot writes the <svg> root (attribute names from StrokeSketch's constants) and the cell-layout comment lines; MultiviewScreenshot and TraceOutlines both use it, so TraceOutlines no longer hardcodes the attribute names. Output text unchanged by construction (same format string and arguments). StrokeSketch.toSvg is in sculpt/ (MESH-91) and should call SketchSvgRoot.open once that lands; its viewBox is scaled, so open would need a viewBox width/height pair then.

Item 8, KDTree3D vs NearestVertex: kept apart. MeshDistance.KDTree3D answers exact squared nearest distance over a raw point cloud (Hausdorff/Chamfer between meshes); NearestVertex buckets a MeshTopology's vertices, returns an id, refuses near-ties and tells coincident copies apart by their faces. MeshDistance has no mesh to hand NearestVertex and needs no tie refusal, NearestVertex needs topology the tree never has.

Item 9, camera projection: Camera3D.projectToPixels gains a (model, x, y, z, width, height, dest) overload that the framebuffer one delegates to; no output change. StrokeSketch.cellPixel is in sculpt/ (MESH-91): after that lands it becomes that overload minus 0.5 per axis (its whole-number pixel centres, as rayThroughPixel takes). SilhouetteHullNode's inner loop stays apart: it premultiplies projection*view once per view and reuses one Vector4f over every lattice point and view (about 16M transforms at resolution 128), where the overload multiplies three matrices and allocates per call.

Item 10, SubdivideMeshNode: its own subdivideOnce copy is gone; it runs SubdivisionMeshNode.subdivide with the new public linear flag (edge midpoints, face centroids, every vertex kept). Positions identical as a point set and face counts equal on petal, tool_quilt and test_function; vertex order changes from vertices-edges-faces to Catmull-Clark's faces-edges-vertices.

Item 10 follow-up: the shared level lives in geometry/mesh/data/ops/MeshSubdivision (subdivide, linear flag, levelCreaseWeights), not in SubdivisionMeshNode, since MeshNodeIndependenceTest forbids one node building another; SubdivisionMeshNode and SubdivideMeshNode both call it. The moved applyCatmullClarkLevel is 250 lines, as it was on master.

Goldens: test/resources/golden/dsl/dungeon_2d.json and dungeon_3d.json re-accepted for the A* tie order (seed 42 2D: 2244 -> 2268 faces). HalfEdgeMeshOps.computeNormals seeds each face's vector-area sum with its first cross, so triangle normals stay bit-identical (HalfEdgeBulkBuildTest compares them bitwise; 0 + -0 would give +0).

Item 1, curvature estimators (user chose the shape operator): SemanticPatchDecomposer reads κ1, κ2 from PrincipalDirectionField and derives the Morse-Smale H = (κ1+κ2)/2, K = κ1·κ2 from them; Meyer's cotangent mean curvature, Gaussian curvature and principal-curvature code (computeMeanCurvature, accumCot, cotAtVertex, computeGaussianCurvature, computePrincipalCurvatures, the barycentric areas) is gone. The angle defect stays for the concavity carve-out. Before/after on block, bolt, fandisk, hand, rocker-arm: patches 277->306, 113->124, 268->288, 203->186, 229->209; Morse-Smale critical points 157->163, 20->17, 32->32, 16->15, 132->118; principal-curvature cut edges Jaccard 0.25, 0.006, 0.18, 0.11, 0.41; union cut set 0.39, 0.85, 0.21, 0.51, 0.71; crest and saddle edges identical; face patch-label purity 0.48, 0.80, 0.91, 0.64, 0.68. The rejected alternative (Meyer magnitudes into the crest/saddle detectors) moved crest edges 0->668 on fandisk and added up to 1351 saddle edges. The two estimators agreed in sign (mean-curvature cosine 0.77-0.97); Meyer read 2.4-3.6x larger, which the p95 thresholds absorb. MESH-91 also edits both curvature files, so a sync after it lands will need a merge there.

Rider (user asked during review): ixdar-cli run-scene --help crashed with 'unsupported format character p', because argparse %-formats help text and run_scene's profile_path doc says %p. ixdar_cli.py now doubles % in every argument help and command summary; all 92 commands' --help print, the CLI's 123 unittests pass.

Rider (user asked during review): MeshNodeViewerScene's startup log no longer advertises P (patch overlay), Shift+P (shader cycle) and D (decomposer toggle); none of the three is bound any more. It now reads 'cycle models with [ and ]'.

Item 10, final form (user asked for one node, code in the node): subdivide_mesh and SubdivideMeshNode are gone, and so is ops/MeshSubdivision. subdivision_surface (SubdivisionMeshNode) holds the level code again and gains a boolean smooth input, default true; smooth=false is the old subdivide_mesh (midpoints and centroids, every vertex kept, creases ignored). The merged node takes subdivide_mesh's 600k-face level cap, documented on the levels socket rather than logged, and its destructive flag and bezier-handle consumes list. birail_loft_ribbon, petal, test_function, tool_quilt and groups/subdivided_cube now call subdivision_surface(..., smooth=false). Their meshes are bit-identical to the two-node version, vertex order included. Graphs outside the repo that call subdivide_mesh need the same rewrite.
Synced onto master after MESH-91 (989460ac). One conflict, SemanticPatchDecomposer: MESH-91 had edited the Meyer curvature code item 1 deletes; kept the deletion.

Item 9 completed: StrokeSketch.cellPixel now calls Camera3D.projectToPixels(model, x, y, z, width, height, dest) and subtracts half a pixel; the overload writes depth only when dest has a third slot (every cellPixel caller passes two). SilhouetteHullNode still stays apart, for speed.

Item 7 completed: the root writer moved into StrokeSketch as svgRoot (with explicit viewBox size and a views table), angleViews and cellLayout; StrokeSketch.toSvg, MultiviewScreenshot and TraceOutlines all call them and SketchSvgRoot is gone (sculpt code no longer has to import from automation). Output text unchanged.

Item 2 completed: MeshSmoothing.ringMean(mesh, activeOf, values, components, countSelf, dest) replaces MeshSmoothing.neighbourMean and DisplacementSum.ringSum. DisplacementSum's normal and drag smoothing average with the vertex counted (the normal pass used to sum; its readers only use direction); its tangential relax takes the neighbour mean directly instead of (sum with self - self) / degree. Measured against master on stroke_sculpt_sphere, stroke_sculpt_head, stroke_crease_sphere and silhouette_hull_skull: sculpt positions move at most 2.3e-4 (sphere, extent 2.31) and 2.6e-6 (head), crease sphere identical. silhouette_hull_skull's smooth_mesh output moves at most 4.5e-7 (float rounding: one sum then a divide, where neighbourMean divided each term), and quad_layout downstream turns that into a different layout (same 4069 vertices and 4067 faces, vertices moved a median 0.044, up to 2.0, on a 1.38-wide skull). Dividing per term instead keeps the skull identical but flips stroke_sculpt_head (up to 6.7 on a 4.66-wide head) through the relax step, so no single rounding order keeps both; both sensitivities exist on master. The benchmark now captures these four graphs and the skull's smooth node.

Item 2 follow-up: MeshSmoothing.ringMean now takes MeshTopology.oneRings() (int[][]) instead of walking the mesh's edges itself; umbrella and DisplacementSum build the rings once before their pass loops. All 30 graph-benchmark outputs bit-identical to the previous run; suite 795/0.
review-summary: Duplicated geometry routines now share one implementation each: the patch decomposer uses only the shape-operator curvature, grid A* runs on Dijkstra, loaders keep HalfEdgeMesh's polygon-area normals, and resampling, simplification, subdivision and SVG roots each have one helper. Two copies drifted apart and gave different results.
